topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the students and outlines the lecture's focus on connecting previously learned immune components to understand inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of Pathogen and Damage Recognition
topics.groupedBecause: The innate immune system detects infection and cellular injury through conserved molecular patterns recognized by germline-encoded receptors across cellular compartments.

topics.label: Pattern Recognition Receptor Families and Signaling Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: Specific receptor families and intracellular complexes transduce pathogen and danger signals into distinct transcriptional and proteolytic inflammatory programs.

topics.label: Leukocyte Trafficking and Acute Inflammatory Responses
topics.groupedBecause: Activated sentinel cells orchestrate the directional migration of immune cells and drive the physiological manifestations of acute inflammation.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The termination of acute inflammation coordinates active tissue repair, while failures to fully resolve the response produce persistent chronic adaptations.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and announces the topic of the subsequent lecture.
